Prologue   Explaining what brought us to the point we find  masrcus .  TWO The Seer  “Sir, I swear he  stole  the pig, if you look you will see it has my brand on it” The overweight man stammered as he stood before the throne his wrenched at the hat in his hands and shifted his feet as he stood there nervously as he glanced around the cavernous hall  “He is a liar, he sold me that pig he did, now he wants it back that’s all Lord, he lies to slander my good name” the second man , standing to the first one’s left yelled almost raising his large calloused hand to hit the accuser. But he couldn’t miss the way the soldiers to either side reached for  there  swords as he did.  So,  he kept his hands at his sides eyeing the soldiers nervously. This was a big man, a man who was used to hard work and getting his way, using his muscles not his brains to ensure he won any argument Galen thought sitting there on the throne, sitting in judgement of the twentieth grievance that morning.  Galen was an old man, he was now the better part of sixty, ancient in these days but the old man still had plenty of life left in him as any rival to his power quickly found out.  He said there his delicate hand, the hand of a scholar, not a farmer stroked the long grey beard his steel grey eyes narrowing at the two.  He didn’t speak for a long time allowing the two men to sweat under his scrutiny. He had already decided the outcome of this before they had even stepped  up. But Galen loved the effect power had on those who had none, he relished the feeling of having complete control over others. Power not money was the only true measure of success as money was just used to buy more power he thought distractedly. The large Merchant let out a quiet whimper pulling Galen from his thoughts and he smiled “I agree this man stole your pig, for that he will  loose  his hand, however I also feel that you might have agreed to sell the animal and then pulled out and for that the pig is confiscated and you are charged twenty  soveriegns  for your crime” he decreed. The man  whose  hand was fated for the cutting block began to sputter and tried to argue before two guards grabbing him under the arms dragged him out.  The Merchant looked to the man and then back to Galen. With a shaky hand he fished out ten gold coins, dropping another five which took him a few moments to collect. He handed the coins to the mouse of a man who appeared from next to Galen, collecting the coin and whispering to the guard to get the pig before the merchant left. The merchant was escorted out bowing and scraping his thank  yous  to Galen as he did. “Niles,  please  tell me  me  we are done this for today?” he asked aggravated . The little man smiled sardonically “we could do a few more but I sense that would have you ordering my head removed” he  said,  and Galen smiled but rolled his eyes. “I must ask my lord, why did you have the thief ’ s hand removed, you know as well as I he didn’t ste a l the pig” Niles whispered to his master. Galen just  smiled  “I was  bored,  and we hadn’t really had a good limb  removal in a few days” he said simply  eliciting  a chuckle from his servant.  Waiving the guards off absently he stood up from the large metal throne and stretched, his back aching from his morning spent in judgement of the villagers.  Retiring to his private chambers  he sighed in relief as he entered the room, his private quarters sat in the top left of the large keep, giving him a view of the small town at the bottom of the hill. He enjoyed looking over the people below giving him the feeling of a deity after all he was the one who decided their face, he thought with a smile. Circling the large dining table, he made his way to the closet next to the large covered bed that sat in the center along the far wall. It took Galen a few moments to remove the uncomfortable velvet robes that he used for official meetings and changing into a simple cotton night gown, he knew he would have to get dressed before his next  meeting,  but he preferred to spend his alone time in comfort. As he left the large  closet,  he noticed the large metal tray on the able and Niles standing next to the door  being as unobtrusive as here, his man servant was always present but never in the way probably the reason he had lasted so many years Galen thought walking over to the table and waiting as Niles approached lifting the lid from the tray and  awaited  his masters approval on the roasted pheasant before him .  Galen nodded approvingly and sat down as Niles served him, the man always wore the same gold robe of his office and Galen sometimes wondered if the man owned more  then  one or just managed to have it cleaned daily. It was never wrinkled nor dirty and  Niles, for as long as Galen could remember smelled of rose and mint as if he had just come from the bath.  Digging into the tender bird he waited as Niles gathered a stack of parchment that had been carefully placed by the door. “My Lord, your spies in the capital have reported back, indeed the queen once again plots to have you removed, as you are the last of what she refers to as the old guard she feels she could be better served with someone who’s loyalty was never to her late husband, the king” Niles stated carefully separating the stack of papers into smaller piles to the left of his Master.  Galen  waited  as Niles finished and retreated to his place next to the  door,  blending  In  with the background as he was so good at doing. This was not the first time the Queen had tried to oust him from the position of Seer of the Province. He did not hold it against her,  in  fact in her position he would have done the same. Galen had served her late  husband,  until he had died under mysterious circumstances. His body had not been cold when the woman assuming power within the hour of his death had sent out the missives replacing every Seer and Lord Protector in the kingdom. In  fact,  she had already had the replacements waiting in the wings. Galen had seen it coming he had spent decades cultivating support and when the letter arrived replacing him with Lord  Crestel , well the young lord had already died by a rather unfortunate accident. Galen had sent his apologies along with letters to the Kings council and a few other Lords, ones  whose  money the Queen needed in order to fund not only the kingdom but  her planned  conquests  at the time. Needless to  say,  he quickly had received a letter reinstating him, the new letter telling him how it had been a mistake and she would never replace just a wise and loyal subject. He thought an ironic smile spreading across his face as he remembered the letter.  He had thwarted numerous plans by the woman to have him removed. The entire council knew she had killed her husband and as his  his   Magesty’s  last ally Galen was a target, he hadn’t been upset about her removal of the king the man had been good for his coffers, Galen’s ability to influence the man’s decisions had made him very rich over the decades. The Queen however was not so easy to manage making her rule, inconvenient he thought reading over the letters that had made  their  way from the capital. He could receive the news sooner using the crystal communication devices, but he didn’t trust that the woman didn’t have people who were able to listen in. He had done it himself Galen had been the one who had discovered that by taking a  shard  from one of the crystals you were able to receive the conversation. He had used it for almost two years until he was forced to reveal his discovery to the council.  He and the queen had been embroiled in a cold war of sorts for the past two years her attention split as the conquest of the closest territories had been her most pressing issue. Now that she had annexed both, removing the ruling families, well there heads anyways he thought smiling. Now she was again focusing on him. The Queen was a lot of things but stupid wasn’t one of  them.  She knew Galen had  influence and he had used it more  then  once to block decisions that would have cost him power or wealth, the two things in this world he coveted more  then  even life itself.  Galen read through the letter that Niles had put at the top of the pile “Really, an assassin?”   he asked arching an  eyebrow  at his servant. Niles smiled bowing his head slightly “I have already dispatched people, it will look like a bandit attack on the road, however my lord you might want to write Lord  Bingam  again and have him reaffirm his support of you, otherwise it might look odd if yet another assassin dies on his way to kill you in a month” Niles said his words wise and his tone adequately subservient. Galen thought it through his steel grey eyes roving over the pages. Information was power and Galen paid handsomely to ensure he was kept apprised of everything going on in the palace. One sheet caught his eye and he reached for it Reading it and then reading it again as if he had not understood the words.  “Niles is this accurate?” he asked glancing up and shooting an annoyed glance at the other man. Niles stiffened but nodded he knew his master’s mood, and this was not off to a good start. There had been more  then  once that Galen had killed in a fit of rage over smaller things Niles reminded himself with a shiver when he thought about it. “I have coordinated ten separate spies, all good reliable professionals but not one can find any more background on the Queen then he already have my lord, it is as if the woman just appeared from thin air” Niles summarized knowing with all six of the lengthy letters said, In a lot of very eloquent  speech, they said absolutely nothing. Galen blew out a breath, When the king had met the lady within a month of her entering court he had fallen in love and quickly after married her. Galen had spent considerable time and resources trying to find out where this woman had come from. Despite his warnings and cautions the King had ignored them .  “I am in love Galen, absolutely content and in love, can’t you just be happy for me” he had said smiling like a buffoon when Galen had visited the capital , begging the King to not marry the woman wait at least until they knew more about her. He had not and now he was dead  shaking his head he looked over the reports saying pretty much what Niles had. Since she had come to the Kings attention, he had sent people all over the territories  triyng  to find any information on her. Lady Victoria had come to court by way of Lord Walser, who conveniently died soon after  introducting  her at court. Victoria was a stunning woman with poise, grace and intelligence. She had graciously dismissed or turned down at least a dozen proposals by many of the courts high lords that was until the King took notice. Then the woman couldn’t get married fast enough he thought bitterly. Every person he had sent out had come back with the same thing, before she had virtually appeared at Lord Walser’s  house,  he had introduced her to his staff as his cousin. Which Galen easily found out was not true, he had also confirmed she was not a spy for any number of the territories surrounding them.  The woman was a mystery and Galen did not like mysteries.  This woman who virtually did  not exist had managed to do what three kings in the past had failed at. Taking the three smaller kingdoms of  Koric  and  Jer  and bringing them to heel. The new “kingdom” had been renamed to  Vikor  in honor of the queen.  The woman was as ruthless as any Lord or King he had known and that coupled with his lack of knowledge made her extremely dangerous. “Write the letter to Lord Bingham, ensure that he reinforces how his displeasure at my demise would cause the spicket of money funding her new army will stop, that should soften her resolve, also get a confession from the inbound assassin and add that to the letter, he can waive it at her should she resist” Galen finished.  Niles bowed his head “I am not sure I will get the message to our people in time , they are already on the road but I will try should he not be able to get the confession do you wish me to create one to send?” he asked and Galen thought about it “Yes” he finally answered his mind racing through the ramifications of the decision as he always did.  Finally,  having gone through all of the  letters,  requests and reports Galen  stood,  stretching as he attempted to remove the knot in his back, the damn thing becoming more a bother the older he got.  As he was dictating a new letter to a consortium of Lords who controlled the mining syndicate within the kingdom one of the servants burst into the room coming to a stop just inside the Lord’s private quarters. He was flushed and out of breath “My Lord, the queen is calling” he finally stammered out. Galen narrowing his eyes as he studied the young man. “The queen  herself? ” he asked the  woman never did anything for herself, if she was actually calling, what the hell could that mean he thought his mind racing as the young man nodded and with a wave from  Galen,  he removed himself from the chambers.  “Niles, with me” Galen said moving towards the door at a brisk pace his face a mask of worry and suspicion.  They quickly left his private quarters heading to the communications room. He stormed the grey stone hall, servants plastering themselves to either side as he passed, no one wanting to incur his wrath should he be held up.  Everyone  had served with him long enough to know the determined look in his eyes would mean pain for any one of them should he take notice and suffer a delay because of them. Niles followed along silently, once in a while shooting a glance and motioning the other servants away as they passed.  At the end of the hall stood a nondescript wooden door, most people would dismiss this particular room as it lacked any  decortations  or items that would note it as important unless you were observant, should you have a keen eye you might notice the large iron reinforced hinges or possibly the large iron locks that numbered three along the door. Galen waited impatiently as the servant on duty unlocked the door from the inside as was the only way this particular door could be opened. It was manned at all times to ensure that any communication that came in was received, transcribed and sent to the proper person who was usually Niles.  Galen entered the room quickly looking over the wall of planks that stood in front of him, holes twelve inches around and  spaced two inches apart covered the wooden planked wall from floor to ceiling each one filled with a cone of stiff parchment and above each hole stood a label signifying which location the speaker was.  The servant bowed as Galen approached the wall, taking the chair that stood before it. The young man pointed to a particular hole and Galen spoke into it. The crystal taking the vibrations and instantly mimicking them miles away in the capital. “Hello Lord  Bor , it is good to hear your voice” came the distinctly female voice despite the tininess and distortion caused by the parchment speaker cone.  The crystal making contact with the stiff parchment and passing on the vibration to the paper amplifying the sound as is emanated out of the receiving crystal.  “ Hello,  your highness, I  apologive  for the wait, what can your humble servant do for you my Queen” Galen said .   G iving the tone just enough deference as not to appear obstinate.  There was silence for a few moments and Galen could image the woman’s face tensing as she listened to the disingenuous response. After a moment she spoke, her tone sounding kind but direct he wondered if she practiced that often and a sneer came over his face but quickly disappeared as he listened to her request.  “Something has come down in your province. we are unsure what it  is  but I need you to send people out to discover what it is, it would have come down in the western part of your territory. It is critical that someone find it and report back what they find” she stated. Galen cocked his head there was stress in her tone, a sense of urgency over something  like this he thought. “What is it that has come down, was it a balloon my Queen” he asked knowing some of the territories including there’s had been experimenting with heated air and silk cloth to make a bucket float, it was something from the old texts that the scientists had gotten to semi work he thought, if it was a balloon was it from  Dever  , were they sending spies over the border he wondered. Niles and he had discussed the Queens plans for the border territories, and he knew they must be nervous after the consolidation of the western part of the territory. There was silence again then finally the queen answered, “I am not sure, but I do need to find out and quickly Galen, can I count on you with this?” she asked knowing full well she could he thought. “Of course, your  Hieness , I will send someone out at once” he said, and the line went dead. Galen sat back shooting a cautious look at Niles who nodded imperceptibly. They said nothing as they left the room and walked back to his private quarters but once the door was shut and Niles had confirmed no servants stood in the hall he turned to his master. “She is lying my Lord” he said and Galen nodded “She knows what it is , but doesn’t want to tell me” he said beginning to pace the floor “Whatever it is , has her incredibly nervous and desperate if she called me to discover it” he said knowing she would never trust him unless she had no choice. She thought that whatever it was would be long gone by the time she sent anyone from the capital so there was a time limit on this he thought.  “Niles, get me Captain Ker at once, I need him and his team to ride out tonight, I need to know what has the queen so scared and more importantly I need to know  whats  out there and if I can use it against her” he finished. Niles nodded and quickly left the room.    Galen walked over to the chair that sat next to the large stone hearth in the room and plopped down into it, his eyes unfocused as he thought through the conversation again.  It could be that the woman is presenting me with the noose to hang her by he thought but for the life of him couldn’t imagine what it could be.  Research into the  derigibles  from the ancient tomes was still early on and they had only gotten a dog to actually hover for more  then  twenty feet.  The use of crystals as the heating element had taken the project to the next level but still it was far from human trials he thought.  He needed to be mindful of what he told  Ker;  the ancient tomes of knowledge were something that most people did not know about they had been passed down through the royal family for ages. Mostly it was descriptions of equipment and devices most amazing and well beyond the understanding of even the most learned scientist or engineer. However when the queen had discovered the existence after rising to the throne, she had quickly gone through them laying out projects and even offering suggestions and descriptions her knowledge was amazing and no one had been able to understand how it was she could know about things like the heated air balloons and black powder as well as metal projectiles that fire from a tube. Galen shook off the train of thought, that was not helpful  now,  now he  had a chance to gain some insight that he was sure she would rather he not have he thought with a malicious smile.  Niles returned a short time later followed by a tall muscular man with greying blonde hair and a scar that ran down his left cheek, the scar Galen mused that the good captain had gotten saving his life. He stood crossing the room in a few long steps. “Captain Ker, it is good to see you my friend, how is your team?” Galen asked by way of greeting but not really caring one way or the other. Ker nodded in answer to his question Galen studied the old Soldier. Ker had served him for two decades and there was no one save Niles that he trusted more. “I have a mission for you Captain and its time critical” Galen began and could see the man stand straighter focusing his entire attention on Galen.  “Something has come down, I am not sure from  where,  but it has landed to the west, I know  its  not a lot of information and it is very time sensitive. I need you to take your team and find it, bring back anything you find and report back as soon as you discover anything. Take one of the communicators with you” Galen finished surprising the older man. Crystal communicators were not handed out lightly in fact he had only ever been issued them a few times in the last decade.  Ker nodded and with military precision spun on his heels and walked out of his Lords Room.  Niles watched him go and turned to Galen “What do you think he will find?” he  asked,  and he could see the curiosity that was probably mimicked on his face too. Galen shook his head “I am not sure , but maybe we might get some answers about the origins of our illustrious and mysterious queen” he  said a smile laden with Malice spread across his features as he thought of getting something he could use on the queen, finally succeeding in putting the damn woman in place.  SEVEN Fugitive Galen sat in his private quarters reviewing the  paperwork,  the life blood of any  bureacracy , it still amazed him the amount of  it   required  to run a territory, much less a kingdom. Nigel entered quietly coming to stand by the door silently waiting until finally Galen looking up motioned for him to speak. “Captain Ker has returned sir” he  said,  and Galen stood excitedly “Show him in” he said  curtly,  and Nigel bowed slightly quickly leaving the room.  Galen walked around the desk, finally now he would get some  anwers  he thought and tapped his foot anxiously until the large old soldier entered his chamber, coming to the middle of the room and dropping to one knee “My Lord, I am here to report” he stated officially. Galen waved his hand  dismisively  “Of course, what did you find” he asked leaning  in with  interest.  Ker  stood,  though slower  than  he would have liked, his legs still recovering from the urgent pace they kept making it back to the keep.  Borik  and  Sharisa  had stayed with the horses allowing Ker to come directly to the keep as was his duty.  The Captain took a  breath,  knowing the news  wouldn’t make  his Lord happy.  “ My lord, We found the site but whatever had been there was gone” he began and could see Galen’s eyes narrow without taking a breath he walked over to the table pulling out the leather pack and began producing items, he hoped this would be enough to bely his oncoming  rage “However, we  did find some items that we believe are related, however we are not sure what most of them are” he finished carefully laying out item after item on the table. Galen looked on in interest his coming rant seemingly forgotten as he moved towards the table, picking up each item and studying it.  Without looking away from the items he spoke though his voice sounding almost distant “Describe for me the where the item was and how you knew it was the location” he commanded and Ker, closing his eyes described the area and the destruction of the trees and then the to the best of his ability the measurements of the indent.  Galen’s eyes never left the table as he moved carefully from one item to the next almost as if  commiting  each one to memory. Ker waited in anticipation of his Lords Response he had been witness to more  then  one unfortunate subordinate who had been on the receiving end of Galen’s rage, it had not ended well for most of them. Finally, mercifully he looked up to study the Captain. “It is not exactly what I would call a success Captain, but you still have done well” he  stated,  and Ker let out a quiet sigh of relief .  “Ker, I need you to…” Galen began and then the door behind Ker slammed open interrupting him. Both men turned to find the disheveled and manic tax collector standing there as Niles attempted to escort him out of the room. “My Lord, My Lord, they are dead all of them” the man yelled, Ker narrowing his own eyes and studying the man, he recognized the look this man was suffering from shock.  He recognized all too well when a man has gone beyond  reason and  seen things his mind could not yet process it shut down giving him a very specific  look.  Stinton  was his name Galen thought, though to be honest he didn’t really keep close attention to his underlings that he left  for  Niles. Looking to Ker he nodded “I can see that Captain” he responded conveying the annoyance and Ker quickly quieted stepping back to allow the Lord Seer to do his job.  “ Stinton , now tell me what happened” he ordered the command cutting through the  man’s   panic.  “My Lord” he said dropping to his knee, his panicked and addled mind remembering where he was.  Galen motioned for him to stand and  Stinton  rose unsteadily to his feet, his face and clothes covered with the damp aftermath of the snow mixed with the soot and ash of his friends.  “Now, what happened”  Galen said  making it more an order then a request.  Stinton  stood there recalling the events that led him there to a stunned group. In the end he collapsed into blubbering. “ Niles  get him out of here” Galen ordered turning to Ker  “Captain,  we will  go see  this man for ourselves ” he said, stepping over to the closet and gathering his coat and boots.  Nodding to the soldier he stepped past Niles leaving him to deal with broken mind of  Stilson . “We leave at once Captain” he said passing Ker, he could see the troubled look on the man’s face but honestly he did not believe the ramblings of a broken man, something had happened but did he honestly think that someone could light people on fire with his mind he scoffed making his way down the stone passages as servants moved to get out of his way.  Exiting the keep he moved to his carriage Ker exited right behind him, nodding to his people to  follow.   Borik  and  Sharisa  exchanged an annoyed glance with each other and began to  dress the horses. Galen waited standing akimbo as he looked around for his carriage driver. “My Carriage, NOW” he bellowed the echo of his displeasure bouncing off of the high walls and ramparts of the old stone structure.  Ker whispered to  Borik  who nodded, getting on his horse and riding out of the keep while servants scrambled and  scraped,  gathering the horses and setting up the Lords Carriage. It took almost thirty minutes as Galen stood there glaring disapprovingly at his people before he was ready to  go.   The group left the compound Ker and  Sharisa  in the lead as they made  their  way past the village and towards the spiraling smoke that marked  their  destination.  Galen sat in his carriage as he  aloud  the soldiers to secure the area before getting the nod from Captain Ker before exiting and walking to the front of the charred building.  Galen stepped  lightly over the charred area passing what was left of the six smoking bodies. “Where is this man, Stinson stated he was here” He said looking to Ker. The Captain shot a look at  Sharisa  who immediately began to canvas the area, stepping around the bodies as she studied the ground.  Galen knew  of her skill and nodded approvingly as he stared in disgust looking at the  thourougly  charred bodies surrounding him. In the distance he could hear the hoofbeats of multiple horses approaching and looked up to see Ker’s other soldier with someone Galen knew well Messenger Veric rode alongside the two quickly riding up to the properly. Veric getting off of his horse, a look of worry and horror across his face “Have you found Orah and Marcus, what happened my Lord” he said looking from body to  body as he searched for what Galen presumed were his friends. “I take it Messenger; you know the residents of this property?” he asked giving the holy man a pointed look.  Veric looked from body to body and  Galen,  not used to repeating himself was about to ask again when Galen Stammered out “Yes, My Lord, but I don’t think these are them” he breathed almost with relief until he took in the smoking ruins of the small cabin. “Aurtus save us” he breathed stepping towards the small house. “What happened here my lord” he  asked,  never taking his eyes off the smoking ruins of the building.  Galen eyed  Sharisa  for a moment studying the woman as she canvased the ground, her blond hair tied into a tight ponytail revealing high cheek bones  and crystal green eyes, she was breathtaking, but Galen new better then to take one like this as a slave or whore, she was a soldier and would quite probably kill him in his  sleep , but then again that might be exciting too he thought a slow grin spreading across his old features as he admired her form.  “My Lord” Veric called breaking him from his thought before his imagination could cause his ancient loins to stir. “Yes Messenger, according to our man  the  man of the residence caused these six men to burst into flames with his will” he said a wry smile replacing the lascivious one from a moment before.  The messenger shot an odd gaze at the Lord Seer but before he could question  it,  it was gone replaced again with worry for his flock and from what Galen could see, his friends. “My Lord, I don’t think this has any connection to the item that fell from the sky, it looks more like a local matter” Ker stated in a low  voice. But  again,  Galen caught that odd gaze from the messenger and just like that it was gone.  Sharisa  stood after examining the area and came over to the Captain, ensuring to address both of them out of respect for Galen’s position he was sure. “Sir, My Lord it appears as if the man collapsed but was carried away, from the depth of the prints, I would say one man carried him off in that direction” she finished and pointed towards the  treeline  to the east.  Galen studied the forest in that direction, he knew it went on for miles before any other signs of civilization appeared. The old Lord stood there staring out over the forest and then turned to the Captain “ Lets  get back to the keep, I want you to send one of your people to Warden’s keep, I want Corliss here by morning.  She  will track the fugitive and we will get back… to other matters” he finished shooting a glance at the Messenger who still stood staring at the cabin. But Galen was sure his look had changed, no longer did he look like the old caring messenger. His face was now critical and assessing and he knew he was seeing something important, his instincts told him that but he was missing something, context he thought this man he had known for a decade as the messenger and leader of this village was gazing at the  grizly  scene like his soldiers would. Not like that of a holy man, “Is everything alright Veric?” he called and as he watched the man’s face changed again morphing into the person he had known, the worry appearing back on his face as he turned to face the Lord Seer. “ Yes,  my lord, I must get back I am sure the townspeople will be concerned and need a calming voice” he said turning to go. Galen  let  him,  studying the man as he walked back to his horse and rode off towards his church. Galen would have to watch him at least that is what his instincts told  him,  and he rarely ignored them.  Turning  back,  he could see  Sharisa  had already made it to her horse and was riding in the direction of Warden’s keep.  The wardens were an order as old as the Seer’s themselves created by the first king of the territories they were charged with bringing  criminal’s  to justice. With a nod Galen returned to his carriage. “ Captain Ker  see that the scene is protected until Corliss arrives, I am sure he will want to survey it” Galen called as the carriage took off back towards the keep. Ker came to rigid attention and saluted the carriage as it left.  Galen had not seen anything that  grizly  in years and in the back of his mind he couldn’t help wondering if the queens strange request and this were not somehow tied together. But he would keep this a local matter until he was sure. No point in giving the queen more ammunition to try and get rid of him he thought. Besides he wanted to take a closer look at those items the Captain had brought back, something about them was familiar as if he had seen some of them before but he couldn’t place his finger on it. But before he reported it back to the  queen,  he wanted to know everything he could about what he was searching for. Something about this had his hackles on end, the urgency and importance of the strange request bothered him and if at all possible he wanted to know if he could use it as leverage, the hag wanted him gone and only his support amongst the court had kept him in power. She had more  then  once tried to have him  assassinated but he had managed to thwart her each time. He was close with the lords of the court that she needed to fund her conquest of the  easter  territories she might hate him because of his allegiance to her late husband but not enough to jeopardize that openly he thought with a smile.  But he also knew he was on borrowed time, once she had completed her conquest and she no longer required the services of those elder lords then she would be free to get rid of him and Galen was no fool, he would find himself at the wrong end of the queens guard the second that happened. Better to have something to use against her as leverage should that  occur,  he thought.  He let his thoughts wander as he watched the sun retreat behind the trees and the wind brought in the cold chill of the evening air as he closed his eyes feeling the burning cold whip across the wrinkle lines of his face.  Messenger  Meric  sat astride his horse as he eyed the Lord Seer’s carriage passing the small village. Anyone who knew the man wouldn’t have recognized him at that moment. The smiling gentle messenger that led the town in weekly prayer was gone. This face, the face that watched the carriage was that of a predator, that of a creature who cared only for the hunt. The twinkle of zealotry shone in his crystal blue eyes as he  mouths  the sentence “Aurtus free us from the demonic  presense  of the fallen” he  whispered,  over and over. But Marcus couldn’t sit here and let this poor girl die he thought his eyes wandering to the kindling that was nestled around a long pole standing erect to one side of the camp.  There had to be something he could  do,  and he thought furiously trying to figure out a way to free this poor girl.  He looked around frantically looking for anything he could find to throw at the damn soldiers, but no that would be just as bad as killing them.  Karibdis  shot an image to  him,  A small group of scouts near the forests  ege . He reached out sensing his  friends’  position, the scouts were on the other side of the camp and Marcus caught his breath as an idea formed.  Closing his  eyes,  he reached out with his mind, searching until he found what he was looking for and smiled as he sent his request.  “In a minute, you are going to go grab her” Marcus said, not opening his eyes Corliss’s head whipped around and he shot his friend a confused look “what?” was all he had time to say before the screaming began. On the far side of the camp more and more screams erupted from the  treeline  and the scouts called out desperately for held.  The camp launched into action as the one in charge pointed to one man to stay with the girl and the rest he  mustered,  and the group of soldiers ran out of the camp and towards the sound of distress.  “Now” Marcus  hissed,  still laying there, eyes closed. Corliss did not wait and jumped to his feet. The soldiers  was  facing away from him, wresting with the young initiate as she struggled to get free, knowing what was to come when the soldiers  returned.  Corliss took off at a full run, pulling a hatched from his belt, he took aim and two steps later launched it at the soldier. The hatchet turned end over end and with a wet thump buried itself into the back of his head.  Corliss ran up to the body and pulled out the hatched, the young  initiage  standing there stunned, unable to move as she was gripped with fear. “Run” Corliss hissed and that was enough to put her into action and she ran out of the camp and into the field, Marcus shot up just as she passed and grabbed her. Corliss nodded and was about to decide what to do with the body when the large black furred profile of  Karibdis  shot by him, grabbing the soldier by the head in his large jaws and dragging him towards the  woodline .  Standing alone in the camp, for a moment he wasn’t sure what to do, then shaking off the moment of shock at the large wolf and his dinner he shot back to Marcus who was still standing there struggling with the young girl. “Move, now” Corliss said, continuing towards the  treeline .  Practically dragging the girl for a few steps, until she realized they were not going back to the  soldier’s  camp but towards the woods. The tree ran as fast as they  could,  making the  treeline  and crashing into it.  Once inside the safety of the brush, Marcus checked the poor girl over. “ Its  okay, I am from the order” he said calming her and checking her for wounds. She had been beaten but could still walk and didn’t seem to be in too much pain, shock yes, but not pain. “Do you know your way back to the keep?” he asked  her  and she nodded, her eyes still vacant as the events of the last hour had not  settled in.  Karibdis  came sauntering up, his muzzle covered in blood and gore and the poor girl just about bolted then, but Marcus hung onto her. “ Its  okay, he is a friend” he said and  Karibdis  came over to sit next to them, putting on his happy puppy face he waited patiently until the girl put a  hand out  and began to scratch his ear. “I am going to have my friend here take you back to the keep, can you walk?” he  asked,  and she nodded. Marcus closed his eyes and shot a series of pictures to the big wolf who responded in the affirmative. “He will lead you back, go with him” he said, trying to get her to safety as soon as possible.  Karibdis  stood and walked a few steps, turning and looking at her expectantly. She rose slowly and followed the large wolf.  Corliss never left the  treeline  he sat there surveying the camp as the soldiers, bloodied and bit came walking back into the camp. Two carried a large dead grey mountain cat. Corliss shot a look at Marcus who smiled “We needed a distraction” he said and then his face fell,  mouring  the cat who gave its life so they could save the girl.  Marcus and Corliss watched as they discovered the missing girl and the missing soldier. The group canvassed the camp. After a few moments one of the soldiers began studying the ground “If he is even a halfway decent  tracker  he will notice my prints” Corliss said cursing himself for not covering them when he left. But the soldier either didn’t see the tracks, or didn’t deem them important, following the drag trail, he pointed to the woods and a small group of soldiers took off in that directing. Corliss, remembering the wolfs muzzle  winced at the thought of what they would find. They waited for an hour as the camp finally settled down and they were sure the soldiers didn’t suspect anything other than odd animal behavior.  Corliss  finaly   moved,  touching his friend and motioning him to follow as they made  there  way around the camp using the  treeline  for cover. They finally made it to the other side, checking the camp once more to see the soldiers packing up and they set off towards Vik for answers.  They began walking as the sun showed itself over the horizon the canopy above keeping the air cooler as they walked in shade. “That was  quickl  thinking back there” Corliss said not looking back as they walked. “I couldn’t leave her to die, so I thought outside the box” he  joked,  using an old corporate motto. Corliss turned back looking at him strangely for a moment and then shook it off. “We should reach the edge of Vik by tonight and then the palace the next day, if there is indeed an army being  readied,  it  wil  be there” Corliss finished. But Marcus already knew the sight of those banners confirmed his worst fear. The Sword of the Faithful was still around and they were working with the queen.  They used the old hunting trails, steering clear of the villages and roads where they might meet people. It took a little longer but be nightfall they were coming to the edge of Vik. It a bit of searching but they finally found a decent place to sleep.  Settling in Marcus turned to his friend “What do you think we will find tomorrow” he asked trying to get a look at the stars  through the canopy “If we are lucky, not a damn thing” he said and they both chuckled. Sleep was slow coming but eventually it did, Marcus again fought through the parade of blood in his dreams until he felt Corliss waking him the next morning. He opened his eyes seeing the beginnings of daylight peeking through the canopy above. “What is it” He said, looking around for the danger. Corliss patted his friend “Nothing, we just need to go” he  said,  and Marcus rose and began packing.  As the sun was continuing to rise, they set  out,  staying to the forest as much as possible and passing fields only after ensuring there was no one in sight. As they got closer and closer to the capital, it began harder to avoid people. The towns became bigger and the trails busier as they passed into the highest concentration of people in the territory.  It was just after midday when they caught there first sight of the tall grey palace looming up over the horizon.  Marcus had to admit it was a breathtaking sight.  The landscape seems to bend to the will of the place, as if the land itself was presenting the castle to the world. They approached cautiously not getting  to  close to the towns they passed and the closer they got to the palace, the more nervous Marcus became.  “There” Corliss  said,  pointing across a field they had walked until midday and then under  Corliss’s  suggestion they started looking for a good vantage point.  The had come to a rise and from here they caught there first sight of the camps.  Corliss turned to his pack, pulling out two pieces of glass and a thick leather sheet. Winding the sheet around the two lenses he tied it off and then Marcus realized Corliss had a Monocular. “Clever” he said smiling at the device Corliss ignored him instead surveying the camp with the monocular as his face deepened into a frown. “Tell me what you make of this” he said handing it over to Marcus.  He gently put it to his eye and began to look at the distant camp. The magnification wasn’t  great,  but it definitely was better  then  looking at it with the naked eye. He surveyed the scene of the camp for a while, watching groups of men and  women training  on the fields near the camp and the smoke from the  smith’s  tent ensuring new weapons daily. “I am guessing about 2 or 3 thousand troops, those barrels near the edge of the camp are probably black powder and they have about half of  there  weaponry  done. I  would say they are still training. From the look of the regiment. They are looking at distance combat” he finished, handing it back to his friend. Corliss gave him an impressed look “I would say the  same” he finished not hiding the surprise in his voice.  Marcus just gave him a pointed look “I was a soldier you know” he commented and then pulled  out a  piece of parchment, scrawling notes and small drawings of the camp. They did this for an hour and realizing they weren’t going to get anything else, The two retreated to the  woodline .  Corliss checking to ensure no one was following.  “We can start back and make some good time before dark, I would rather put some distance between us and this place” Corliss said, looking back towards the profile of the palace his face covered in a worried expression.  They spent Three days retracing there steps back towards the order by the time they reached the edge of the forest that would take them back to the keep, a large furry wolf waited on a rock, as they approached Marcus smiled as  Karibdis  wagged his tail and smiled at them. “Hey boy” Marcus said, giving his head a scratch. They rested for an hour and the made  there  way back to the keep.  As they approached Marcus was pleased to see two guards on duty outside the door. They were quickly ushered in and shown to the main meeting room. Kalman and Avram came rushing in ten minutes later. Kalman took one look at  there  faces and his own face  fell. “They are building an army  aeren’t  they” he said as a statement not a question.  Marcus nodded. “They have two or three thousand troops, but Kalman the flags it’s the Sword and they have barrels of black powder.” He finished and Marcus didn’t think it  possible,  but the man’s face fell even further.  Avram nodded “Get cleaned  up,  meet us down in the crafting hall” he said and motioned for Kalman to join him. Marcus was beat, but they still had the council to deal  with,  so he returned to his room and cleaned up, putting on a fresh pair of clothes helped his mood slightly.  He met Corliss  in  the hall and the two ventured down into the keep until they reached the level where the hall was. As they turned the corner, Marcus could hear the bustling activity going on ahead and the closer he got to the room, the more excited he was. Walking in he stopped, seeing the Apprentices running  around,  the forge at full heat, the crushers going as they consumed the material and turned the lot into equipment, armor and weapons. “This is the war machine” Marcus said absently. Corliss shot him an odd look and then noticed Kalman waiving them over.  Approaching Marcus noticed the small line of swords in a newly built rack. “I had to call in some help, but we are making process, I  would say in the next thirty days we should have enough to equip an army. All three forges in the keep are working overtime, plus there was a supply of older swords and Magi  amor  behind the supplies over there” he said pointing and smiling. “That’s about all the time we might have from the look of it, we need to start training people as soon as possible, which means, we need to talk to the council” Marcus finished wincing at his own words. Kalman nodded “There is already  whisperes  about what we are doing, if the council don’t know they will soon, so yes  its  time to go before them. But you will have our support” Kalman stated and Marcus knew what that meant.  The guilds wielded a lot of influence in the keep, there support was no small thing.  Corliss tapped him on the shoulder “I am going to tell  Agata  we are back safe” Said his friend, looking more like a little  love sick  teenager then the rugged warden he was. Marcus smiled and motioned for him to go.  Kalman shook his head but said nothing.  “We will get the meeting ready, but it won’t be easy my friend” Kalman said. Marcus nodded “If we fail here, it could mean the end to all of us my friend” he answered.  FOURTY - FIVE Training…     Ardsley  stolled  through the training grounds, the sun beat down on his bald head causing him to wipe it so often to keep the sweat down.  The  Emmisary  of Aurtus Udo  Conraden  walked next to him. His face still partially covered in bandages after the battle at the City in the Trees the young man looked content as he spied the training soldiers on the field. “You seem pleased” Lord Ardsley said eyeing the other man warily the more time he spent with the holy man the more he came to distrust him. There was an agenda here and one that had nothing to do with the queen.  Udo’s smile brightened though Ardsley could see the wince when he had pushed it too far “The training is coming well, we are still recruiting within the next three months we will be four thousand strong and just about ready to put the army to use” he stated continuing to walk along the camp’s  thouroughfare .  Lord Ardsley nodded; they had done incredibly well in that department. The writs of service had gone out and over ninety percent had yielded recruits, though it wasn’t like the queen had given them a choice. The writ was mandatory and anyone who refused was levied  heavily to the point of bankruptcy. The weapons were coming along well, they had smiths building the more traditional swords and crossbows and the specialists from the church working with the bolts and the explosive power. Then there  was  the crystal dust, Udo had  insited  it get put into everything from the swords while they were smelted and the arrows all the way to the armor itself. He would not explain why he would just say  it was  required. It didn’t harm  anything,  and Ardsley thought it was some church  ritual,  so he allowed it.  They walked a little further in silence, both men  reguarding  the training  recruits.   Urdo  stopped to watch them “This is a mighty army my friend, it will be used to do  Aurtus’s  will, this army will be a holy army indeed” the man beamed, he was so focused on the soldiers that he missed the narrowing of Ardsley’s eyes. Lord Ardsley had heard this talk from the emissary before. What plan do you have for this army and why do I think it does not include the queen he thought still looking at the man as he continued to beam at the troops like a proud father watching his son taking his first steps.  “It will be a grand army for our queen” Ardsley said  pointedly,  continuing to watch the man carefully. His smile faltered for only a moment, but Ardsley caught it “Yes, of course” he answered and turned, continuing to walk.  They parted was at the supply tent.  Urdo  begging off that he still needed rest after his ordeal and Ardsley wanting to check on the status of the food supplies for the troops.  An hour later Ardsley sat in his little house and staring out the window that looked over part of the camp. His daughter came over setting a bowl of steaming hot stew in front of him “You need to  eat;  you won’t  be any  use to anyone should you become sick father” she gently chided. He nodded picking up the spoon and slowing sipping the broth until it cooled a bit. But this was enough to stop Loraine from worrying at him.  She came and sat down across from  him;  her own bowl cradled in her palms. “ Whats  wrong, something has been eating you these past few days” she asked, looking up at her father and when he turned to her, he could see the worry on her face. He smiled reassuringly at her. Nothing, I just have reservations about our  Emisarry  that is all” he  said,  taking another bite of the stew.  Lord Ardsley shook his head, trying to organize the myriad of thoughts that came to him when thinking of  Urdo . Since his arrival the man had rubbed him the wrong way. But lately when the man mused or thought no one was paying attention some of his statements worried him. He finally looked up to see Loraine still waiting for him to answer. “I think he might have another  agenda,  one he has not shared with the queen” he finally said for the first time putting into actual words his thoughts on the man.  She looked at her father her expression serious “Have you shared this with the queen?” she asked  him  and Ardsley shook his head. “No,  Its  just a feeling my dear, not worth bothering her over” he said getting up from the table. “I still have many  things to do before the day ends,  ill  be in late” he said leaning over and kissing the young woman on the head. She had spent so much time  worring  over him, she had not found time to live her life and that among  everything saddened  him. A young girl should not fuss over her ailing father, she should be out having fun and enjoying her youth.  He stepped out into the  mid day  sun and walked over to the command tent.  He entered to find Lord Rogan standing over the two men as they reviewed ledgers of supplies. “Lord Rogan, I thought I smelled something foul” he said the other man looking up, half his body still swathed in bandages and smiled at Ardsley. “Lord Ardsley, always so good to see you, how is that lovely daughter of yours” he asked with a sneer. Ardsley just shot him a withering look. “What are you doing here Rogan, this isn’t your project nor are  you  military” he asked pointedly. Anytime Rogan showed up it meant he wanted something Ardsley had known lords like him all his life, the only thing they served were themselves.  Rogan had been elevated, not highborn and that already put him on shaky ground with Ardsley who believed the only way to be a true noble was to be born into it. But Rogan’s parents had been  mid level  merchants at best, the queen however had seen fit to elevate this man’s status. Giving him land and title, since that moment he had spent every second of the day trying to  aquire  more and more of both.  “Ensuring the queens coin is put to good use that is all Ardsley nothing to concern yourself about” he said smiling, then slapping the  young man in front of him on the back he walked out of the tent. Ardsley waited a few moments ensuring that the other  man was  indeed gone. After a moment Ardsley was ushered in to find the queen standing by the window, the one that overlooked his troops. “How goes the  training my  lord” she asked pleasantly. Ardsley walked in and knelt, offering his respect to her position. He hated  politics;  he had always been a much better soldier he thought.  “Well, I am waiting” she said  turning to face the older man her gaze critical, but not hard. “I am not sure how to say this, so I am going to just say it, I have no proof, only suspicions my queen” he began, taking a breath before continuing. “I think that our emissary might have his own designs when it comes to the  army and I fear they don’t align with yours” He said watching her as he finished his statement. At first the queen said nothing, she stood  there  arms crossed looking out towards the window as the sounds of soldiers training wafted in through the window. “I appreciate you sharing your suspicions with me Lord Ardsley” she began, looking back at him and taking a step closer. “I am sure the church has  there own  ends to this army, but this is my army and I will not allow it to be  ursurped   by  a  bunch of messengers of Aurtus. Ardsley nodded “Yes, yes my queen” he stammered bowing as he began stepping back towards the entrance. “ Oh  and Ardsley” she said turning away from him. “Yes” he said stopping by the door. “Do try and play nice with Lord Rogan” she simply stated and then waived him off.  Ardsley left the queens meeting chambers and walked as fast as he could out of the building. He never liked dealing with her, not since she had personally banished him. But it almost sounded like she knew the church was planning something  and didn’t care he thought. But that  couldn’t be  right could it? He wondered.  Ardsley buried himself in the normal training routine for the day, trying to put the meeting with the queen as far behind him as possible.  The troops were coming along nicely, the ranged training with the new crossbows was coming along nicely the soldiers getting better and better  everyday  practicing shoot, reload, shoot over and over. As the sun set over the training grounds and the light began to fade. Ardsley walked along the main path of the camp, heading back to his house where he knew Loraine would  be  up with dinner waiting. Passing by the supply house he spied a few soldiers loading barrels of the explosive powder onto a small cart.  Arsdley  looked but didn’t recognize any of them. Walking over and getting closer he now saw the emblem of the  queens  personal guard emblazoned on  there  tunics, that’s odd he thought stepping up to the men. “Can I help you gentlemen?” he asked and the one who was supervising turned. “Lord Ardsley, no sire we have it well in hand” he said nodding to him and turning back to the soldiers loading. “ What exactly  do you have well in hand?” he asked. Letting a little severity into his tone, he did not like the look of this.  “Oh, let them work Ardsley” came a familiar voice from behind the cart, after a  moment Rogan  appeared all smiles as he walked towards Ardsley. “Isn’t it past your  bed time  my lord, maybe you should go home and let that lovely daughter of yours serve you dinner” and there was that sneer  again. Ardsley would like nothing more at that moment then to punch it off of his face, but instead he smiled. “Well, Lord Rogan, how is it I always find you wherever I smell a rat” he asked his tone jovial  but  the  intent was clear. Rogan did not take the bait “We are here on orders from the queen, nothing you need to concern yourself about” he said waiving the man away dismissively. Ardsley was about to call the camp guards over but paused, remembering what the queen had said Play nice with Rogan. Swallowing his pride and the anger this man always seemed to illicit, Ardsley smiled “Of course you are, I will leave you to it then” he answered and with a  slight bow, he turned and strolled off towards his house, biting his tongue as he did. But he had caught the disappointment in the other man’s face, he had been spoiling for a fight. As he  walked,  he thought about everything that had been happening and he still felt as if everyone was leaving him out of the bigger picture, like there was something he was not seeing even  through  he was right in the middle of it. Why did the queen want barrels of  powder,  where the hell  was  she taking it he  wondered? FOURTY - SIX The Council…     Marcus stood in the familiar place outside the council’s chambers, he had waited here for nearly an hour waiting for the doors to open. Councilor  Torin  looked taken aback for a moment then pressed on “This proves nothing, you want us to take all of our production and push it towards a war footing, to turn our initiates and the magi into soldiers to fight some make believe enemy  purly  for your own vanity” he yelled .
